text: Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League Boxing Day fixture, as Sheffield United host fellow bottom-three strugglers Luton Town at Bramall Lane.
Having won just 9 points from their 18 games so far, Sheffield United are propping up the table from 20th and sit a hefty seven points behind Everton in 17th.
Returning manager Chris Wilder won his first game back in charge of the Blades, but was denied a second victory in three by Nicolo Zaniolo's 97th-minute equaliser for Aston Villa four days ago.
18th-placed Luton are still four points from safety and have won just once in four games, but that victory was a hugely deserved one over Newcastle last time out.

The Hatters were impressive throughout that 1-0 win at Kenilworth Road, and having pushed both Arsenal and Manchester City all the way in recent weeks, Rob Edwards’ side will certainly fancy their chances against a side two places and three points below them in the table.
The Blades came within seconds of a crucial victory at Villa Park, and Chris Wilder makes four changes to his XI looking to continue the momentum with some fresh legs.
James McAtee and Gustavo Hamer both come into midfield, Oli McBurnie leads the line up front, and Anel Ahmedhodzic wears the captain’s armband from centre-back.
Cameron Archer, whose goal looked to have wrapped up the points against his former club, starts from the left flank, looking to support McBurnie in attack alongside McAtee.
Ryan Giles replaced Issa Kabore out wide for Luton against Newcastle, and with the Burkinabe wing-back absent from the squad altogether, starts in his place in the visitors' only change.

He and fellow wideman Alfie Doughty were crucial to the Hatters seeing out the points last time out, with the pair set to provide Jacob Brown, Elijah Adebayo and goal-scorer Andros Townsend with plenty of ammunition in the final third.
The teams head out onto the pitch at Bramall Lane, and we'll be underway at this famous old ground in just a matter of moments!
Lokonga will kick off for the Hatters, and we are up and running on Boxing Day in South Yorkshire!
Sheffield United have lost just one of their last seven league games against Luton, though that defeat did come at Bramall Lane in the two sides' most recent meeting in March of last season.
Townsend switches the play wide to Doughty, who beats his man before crossing from the right.
Ahmedhodzic gets across at the far post to glance the ball away from danger, but comes off second-best in the process.
Luton break at speed after cutting out a chance and Doughty sets off on the counter-attack.
He looks to whip in another cross from the right, but Brooks slides in to put the ball behind for the game's first corner.
Luton beat Sheffield United 1-0 away from home in the Championship last season, but have never won back-to-back league visits to Bramall Lane before.
Giles plays the ball forward to Adebayo in the box who tries to take on the defence, but finds himself crowded out and Baldock's intervention gives the Blades a goal-kick.
Forward come Sheffield United as Hamer passes inside to Archer on the edge of the box.
He tees up Vinicius to shoot first-time, but the Brazilian's 25-yard effort is easily blocked by Osho.
BLOCKED!!! Hamer dribbles into the area and opens up his body to shoot goalwards, but Osho gets in the way and deflects his strike behind for a Sheffield United corner!
McBurnie rises at the far post and heads towards goal, but the ball hits him via a deflection, looping up and over the bar before landing on top of Kaminski's net!
Adebayo gets the run on Ahmedhodzic after winning the battle for a loose ball, but he's tugged back and tripped by the Sheffield United captain, who is booked as the referee blows for a free-kick.
Doughty's free-kick is met by a weak punch from Foderingham that does little to clear the danger, but Barkley can't make anything of his follow-up shot and the ball is thumped away.
CHANCE!!! Adebayo races onto the ball from Brown's flick-on into the box, but Foderingham closes the gap quickly and forces the striker too wide to keep it in the field of play!
GOOOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! Luton lead at Bramall Lane!!! After scrappily clearing the ball away from their own end, the Hatters finally bring it down on halfway and Lokonga passes wide to Doughty.

The wing-back then sets off on a remarkable run into the box, beating Robinson around the outside before smashing a low shot that goes through the legs of Foderingham and into the back of the net!!! 1-0 to the Hatters, and it comes from a player who is just getting better and better with every passing week!
Lokonga's pass gave Doughty the space he needed to carve out that chance, and the wing-back certainly did that with a sensational run and finish!
The Blades look to respond immediately as Baldock hurls a long throw into the Luton box, and after it's initially cleared, Archer's cross back into the middle is headed behind by Mengi for a corner.
This is only the second time that Luton have taken the lead in a Premier League game away from home, also doing so in September at Everton.
It's also the earliest the Hatters have found the net so far this season.
SAVED!!! Townsend bursts past Trusty and hangs up a cross towards the far post, but the target Adebayo can't get enough power behind his header and Foderingham makes the save!
Osho slides in to divert McBurnie's dangerous cut-back behind for a corner, but the hosts can't make anything of their set-piece as the delivery is headed clear at the front post.
Barkley can't pick out a shot or cross from the left byline, so cuts the ball back to Lokonga on the edge of the box.
He lets fly from 20 yards, but Robinson gets in the way to block.
Luton have won 11 of their last 14 away league games against sides from Yorkshire, keeping a clean sheet in nine of those victories.
However, as a top-flight side, they’ve not won in Yorkshire since November 1987 (2-0 v Sheffield Wednesday).

SAVED!!! Osho's foul on McBurnie gifts the hosts a free-kick right on the edge of Luton's box, and Hamer's curling strike from the dead-ball situation is heading for the far corner until Kaminski dives across to tip it just wide of the upright!
WIDE!!! Brooks does well to win possession and bring the ball down just outside Luton's box, and lets fly with a low half-volley which he drags just wide of the far post!

WIDE!!! The Blades go close once more!! McAtee rides one challenge down the right before cutting inside and shooting with his left foot, unleashing a curling effort that has Kaminski sprawling before whistling just inches beyond the upright!
Sheffield United’s last Boxing Day victory in the top-flight came against Luton Town in 1990, a 1-0 win at Kenilworth Road.
Since then they’re winless in six such matches, losing four and failing to score on five occasions.
Robinson's long throw into the box is cleared by Luton, but Hamer recovers possession on the edge of the box.
He picks his spot and shoots from just inside the area, but it's an easy enough effort for Bell to block.
BLOCKED!!! Luton come forward at speed as Adebayo finds Doughty wide to his right.
The goalscorer cuts inside looking for a second goal, but Brooks blocks his shot behind for a corner!
WIDE!!! Barkley meets Doughty's delivery from the corner, but can only send his glancing header whistling past the near post!
Luton keep the ball brilliantly as they look to engineer a chance in the final third.
Lokonga is too quick for Hamer, releasing a pass before being clattered late by the Sheffield United midfielder, who is promptly shown a yellow card.
Townsend strikes the Hatters' free-kick, but sends his effort straight into the Sheffield United wall.
Barkley's onto the rebound and goes for goal first-time, however his attempt also fails to convince and it's a comfortable save for Foderingham!
After Giles makes a vital clearance to send the ball put for a throw, Robinson launches another into the box.
McBurnie gets the flick-on, but Bell is there to hoof the ball away at the far post!
WIDE!!! A second successive Robinson throw-in is nodded clear, but only as far as Brooks on the edge of the box.
He lets fly with a fizzing effort towards goal, but it takes a nick and bounces just wide of the far post for a Sheffield United corner!
We're into one additional minute of added time as an end-to-end first 45 draws to a close in south Yorkshire.
Trusty gets on the end of Hamer's delivery from the corner, but his near-post header is put well over the top!
HALF-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 0-1 LUTON TOWN.

It's advantage Luton at the halfway stage, scoring an early opener and doing their upmost to retain their lead for the second game running! The Hatters started brightly and took the lead in superb style after half-chances at each end.
Doughty's mazy run from the right flank was sublime in itself, but his low finish that squeezed beneath Foderingham and into the net was even better.

events.action: squeezed beneath Foderingham and into the net

text: Luton could have extended their advantage, with Adebayo and Barkley missing close-range headers and Doughty having another effort blocked, but the visitors had to withstand a late onslaught from Sheffield United at the other end.
Kaminski saved brilliantly from Hamer's free-kick, with McAtee and Brooks (twice) firing wide from the edge of the box as the hosts pushed for an equaliser.
Luton have withstood the challenge so far though, and are on course to close the gap on Everton above them to just one point.
Barkley has once again been running the show for Luton in midfield, having three attempts on goal and completing seven final-third passes in that first half.
He's created one big chance from those passes, won eight of his 12 duels including three dribbles, and has turned possession over on four occasions so far.
Engine.

Max Lowe will come on for hosts as we gear up for the start of the second half, replacing Brooks in a change that will likely see Hamer and Archer occupy more central roles in Sheffield United's midfield and attack.
McAtee gets the game back underway for the Blades, as the second half begins at Bramall Lane!
Sheffield United have failed to score a first-half goal in 16 of their 19 games so far this season, the most of any side in the Premier League.

CHANCE!!! Baldock's teasing cross is whipped right into the middle with options arriving in the six-yard box, but Luton defender Mengi volleys it just over the top of his own crossbar for a corner in a real hearts-in-mouths moment for the Hatters!
Mengi's long ball forward is brought down well by Adebayo, but he's crowded out after cutting inside to shoot and can't make anything of his chance in the box!
BLOCKED!! Archer's cut-back is met by Lowe arriving in the box, but Lokonga gets in the way of the substitute's first-time shot and makes a timely block!
Brown skips past a challenge before crossing into the six-yard box, but his final ball is far too close to Foderingham at his near post and the Sheffield United 'keeper duly collects.
Only Arsenal, Everton, and Newcastle (all 14) have had more different Premier League goalscorers this season than Luton's 12.
Hamer is teed up on the edge of the area with Luton holding their defensive shape well, however the Dutchman snatches at his shot and sends a poor effort looping well over the crossbar.
Baldock cuts inside from the right and links up with McAtee ahead of him, but Brown's attempted clearance from the return ball ricochets off the Blades' right-back and into the gloves of Kaminski.
SAVED!!! Townsend cuts onto his right foot and pulls the trigger from 20 yards, but the curling finish is made to look ordinary by Foderingham's comfortable save!

OVER!!! A poor pass from Vinicius is cut out by Townsend and the winger sets off on a forward run to the edge of Sheffield United's box, standing up the defence before sending a well-struck effort beyond Foderingham's reach and over the crossbar!
GOOOOOOOAAAAALLL!!! The hosts are level!!! Archer chests down a high ball for McAtee and the midfielder surges forward into Luton's box.

Lokonga and Bell both slide in to dispossess the Manchester City loanee and knock him off-balance, but McAtee is still able to get the ball to McBurnie and the striker rifles it into the bottom corner!!! 1-1 in the scrappiest of fashions at Bramall Lane, but the Blades won't care one jot!

events.action: rifles it into the bottom corner

text: McAtee's run there left Luton sprawling, as was shown in the desperation of Bell's challenge, and his awareness to find McBurnie while on the ground allowed the Scotland striker to finish off a bizarre equaliser for the Blades!
There have been 10 previous Boxing Day games between promoted sides in English top-flight history, with the home side remaining unbeaten in all 10.

The most recent such clash was a 1-0 win for Aston Villa against Norwich City in 2019-20, and Sheffield United will be confident that they can build on that equaliser to complete a second-half comeback in this one.
Nine of McBurnie's 10 Premier League goals have come at Bramall Lane.
Among players with 10+ goals in the competition, only Neal Ardley (92 per cent, 11 of 12 at Selhurst Park) has scored a higher proportion at a single stadium.
Bell advances into the final third to link up with Giles on the left wing, but his cross to the far post is plucked out of the sky by Foderingham.

GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAALLL!!! The Blades have turned it around here!!! McBurnie keeps a cleared Baldock cross alive with a brilliant cut-back from the byline, and after neither McAtee nor Archer can turn it goalwards from close range, the captain Ahmedhodzic arrives in the box to side-foot the ball into the far corner!!! An unbelievable last 10 minutes have seen Sheffield United go from 1-0 down to 2-1 up, and Bramall Lane is absolutely rocking!
The second of two scrappy goals in quick succession warrants a VAR check for a possible foul, but there's nothing doing in that regard and so Ahmedhodzic's strike will stand!
Having seen their 1-0 lead evaporate in the last few minutes, Luton make a double change in the final third, with Carlton Morris on to lead the line in place of Adebayo.
Luton also throw on Chiedozie Ogbene in a bid to get back into this game, with the Irish international replacing Giles out wide.
Meanwhile, Anis Ben Slimane comes on for Sheffield United, replacing the booked Hamer in the heart of their midfield.
McBurnie's causing more problems as he holds up a throw-in before playing Lowe in behind the defence, but Osho gets across in cover to make the clearance and prevent a corner being conceded.

GOOOOAAAALLL!!!! We're level once more thanks to an unfortunate own goal!!! A Luton free-kick comes to nothing but is soon crossed back into the area by Morris, and Robinson climbs high looking to glance it away from danger but the ball hits the back of his head, deceiving Foderingham and nestling in the bottom-left corner!!! 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go, and this game is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down!
Baldock is booked amidst the chaos of that own-goal, with the referee not happy with something said to him by the Blades' right back.

Luton bring off their goalscorer Doughty after getting back on level terms, with Mads Andersen introduced both in an effort to keep things tight at the back, and provide options for set-pieces in the final third.
Robinson's frustration continues as he throws Ogbene to the ground while contesting a loose ball with the Luton substitute, and he's shown a deserved yellow card for that rash challenge.
GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!!! Another own goal puts Luton back in front!!! This mind-boggling game takes yet another twist, as Bell's throw-in is collected by Morris.

He beats his marker and cuts the ball back into the middle, but it takes a wicked deflection off Ben Slimane and loops beyond both Foderingham and Lowe to find the top corner!! 3-2 to the Hatters in the strangest circumstances yet, and with just under 10 minutes to go, how much more madness can possibly occur before the full-time whistle goes here?
Sheffield United have scored two own goals in a single Premier League game for the very first time, and have now conceded 16 overall in the final 15 minutes of their games so far this season!
Pelly-Ruddock Mpanzu's on for Luton, and he's replace Andros Townsend as Rob Edwards tries to keep hold of his side's slender lead.
The Blades make a triple change in a bid to throw the dice and rescue this game, with Oliver Norwood replacing Vinicius at the base of their midfield.
Archer's also brought off despite scoring in the latter stages last time out, and William Osula enters proceedings in the final third for the Blades.
Robinson's had a last few minutes to forget, to say the least, and Rhian Brewster replaces him with Chris Wilder going all-out-attack for the final throws of this pulsating contest.

SAVED!!!! Ben Slimane and Osula combine in the box with a variety of headers, and the latter unleashes a wild overhead kick from a tight angle which Kaminski does well to get down to and tip wide of his near post!
Luton have won three of their last five league games on Boxing Day, having been winless in seven such matches before this.
Can they hold on to make it four in six?
EIGHT added minutes to play at Bramall Lane, and from what we've seen so far in this wild second half, hold on to your hats for whatever madness is set to unfold!
OVER!!! The Blades work the ball from left to right and McAtee finds Baldock on an underlapping run.
He cuts it back to Ben Slimane arriving in the box, but his first-time finish is sent looping inches over the bar!
A rather harsh corner goes against Mengi despite him not appearing to have touched the ball, but the defender's there at the near post to head Norwood's delivery well away from danger.
Norwood catches Mpanzu very late indeed with a poor challenge, and it's one that earns the veteran Blades midfielder a yellow card.
A half-cleared Lowe cross falls for Ahmedhodzic 20 yards from goal, but the defender can't repeat his heroics from earlier on as his volley is easily blocked by the Luton defence.

There's plenty being discussed on the touchline between Morris, Luton boss Rob Edwards and referee Sam Allison, but the issue is eventually dealt with and we're back underway - you'd imagine that'll be a few extra seconds added onto the end of the eight minutes.
Bell is penalised late on for a body-check on Norwood, and Blades goalkeeper Foderingham comes forward for what could be the hosts' last chance here!
The initial free-kick is cleared by Luton but Norwood gets a second bite of the cherry and crosses back towards the far post.
Ben Slimane nods it down for Trusty in the middle, but the USA defender's attempt at a half volley is skewed high and wide of the target as the full-time whistle goes!
FULL-TIME: SHEFFIELD UNITED 2-3 LUTON TOWN.

Well, where on earth to start with that one? Luton win 3-2 amidst anarchy at Bramall Lane, seeing their own lead slip midway through the second half before two own-goals in four minutes gifted them the points at Sheffield United's expense!! The Blades meant business in the second period and finally broke through just after the hour mark, McBurnie lashing home after McAtee kept the ball alive in the Hatters' box.
Within eight minutes, the hosts had turned the scoreline on its head, Ahmedhodzic popping up to finish off a similarly scrappy chance after Archer and McAtee failed to convert.

Heading into the final 15 minutes with a 2-1 lead, Sheffield United proceeded to implode in spectacular fashion, Robinson accidentally heading into his own net amidst a flurry of substitutions and yellow cards.
Play had barely got going again before Morris' cross hit Ben Slimane and somehow found its way into the far corner, re-establishing Luton's advantage and leaving the Blades crestfallen.
Late chances for Osula and Ben Slimane both went awry as the hosts desperately chased a deserved equaliser, but Luton held out to claim all three points and secure a second win in a row.

A game that was as mad as a hatter ends in favour of the Hatters themselves, leaving Sheffield United's side rooted to the foot of the Premier League table, and taking Luton just one point away from climbing out of the relegation zone.
